name: Eight-state exact-weld / permanent-reader-equivalence finite witness (domain distinction invisible to any finite-horizon reader)

statement.latest: S=\{0,1\}^3,\ D=\{0,1\}^2,\ F(a,b,c)=(1-a,b,1-c),\ F_D(a,b)=(1-a,b),\ q_D(a,b,c)=(a,b),\ O(a,b,c)=b=O_D(q_D(a,b,c)).\quad q_D\circ F=F_D\circ q_D\ \text{and}\ O=O_D\circ q_D\ \text{hold exactly (exact weld)}.\quad\text{For } z=(0,0,0),\ z'=(1,0,1):\ z\sim_{O,L}z'\ \forall L<\infty,\ \text{yet}\ Q(q_D(F^kz))\ne Q(q_D(F^kz'))\ \forall k\ge0\ \text{where}\ Q(a,b):=a.
statement.note_ascii: 8-state system (2^3 states), domain 2^2 states. F flips coords 1 and 3, fixes coord 2. qD/O project as declared. The exact-weld identities hold on all 8 states (brute-force checked) and F^2=Id (period-2, checked to k=9999 and proved by the flip structure). Witness pair z=(0,0,0), z'=(1,0,1) is reader-indistinguishable (O never differs) at every finite horizon L, while the domain question Q(a,b)=a differs forever. Conclusion: exact domain-dynamics welding plus exact reader-factorization does NOT imply finite-horizon reader decidability of an arbitrary domain question -- a separate bridge theorem is required per domain question, not inherited for free from an exact weld.

name: Global finite-interval continuation for the retained-turbulence relaxation-inertia ODE (existence, uniqueness, boundedness on every finite horizon)

statement.latest: \text{Given }\tau_R\dot I_R+L_RI_R=S_R+\eta_R\ (\text{weld/P.05.v1}),\ \text{with}\ m<\infty,\ \tau_R>0,\ L_R\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\ \text{fixed},\ G_R:=S_R+\eta_R\in L^1_{loc}([0,\infty);\mathbb R^m):\quad I_R(t)=e^{-tL_R/\tau_R}I_0+\frac1{\tau_R}\int_0^te^{-(t-s)L_R/\tau_R}G_R(s)\,ds\ \text{is the unique absolutely continuous solution on every finite interval},\quad \|I_R(t)\|\le e^{t\|L_R\|/\tau_R}\left(\|I_0\|+\frac1{\tau_R}\int_0^t\|G_R(s)\|\,ds\right)\Rightarrow\sup_{0\le t\le T}\|I_R(t)\|<\infty\ \forall T<\infty.
statement.note_ascii: Variation-of-constants solution of the linear ODE tau_R dI_R/dt + L_R I_R = G_R (G_R := S_R+eta_R). Existence+uniqueness+global (all finite T) boundedness follow from standard linear ODE theory given finite dimension m, tau_R>0, fixed finite L_R, and G_R locally integrable -- no smallness, no special spectrum, no PDE input required. Corollary: if L_R=L_R^T is positive-semidefinite, ||e^{-tL_R/tau_R}||_2<=1 and the bound tightens to an energy-type estimate (||I_R(t)||^2 <= ||I_0||^2 + (1/tau_R) int_0^t ||G_R(s)||^2 ds). Consequence for the Navier-Stokes readout dialogue: a hypothetical continuum breakdown (Sigma_NS=1) does NOT, by itself, force a retained-turbulence-layer blow-up (Sigma_R=1) as long as the retained model's own regularity hypotheses H_R(T*) (finite m, tau_R>0, fixed finite L_R, G_R locally integrable up to T*) continue to hold -- any theorem transferring continuum blowup onto this retained layer must show one of those hypotheses itself fails at breakdown, which is a separate, unaddressed claim.

This is the SAME reading, not a variant -- weld/P.05.v1 is cited directly for the equation itself; this proposal registers only the NEW continuation/boundedness theorem about that equation's solutions, which weld/P.05.v1's own entry does not state or claim (its coq_status is open_prop with no continuation result recorded).

L_R here is the same retained graph-Laplacian-type operator rooted at EQ-008 (L_R := D_W - W); this proposal's boundedness/contraction results (Corollary 6.2 in the source, positive-semidefinite case) are exactly the kind of use docs/L_R_SPECTRAL_CEILING_AND_FLOOR.md's ceiling/floor template is written to bound generally -- a finite ceiling on ||L_R|| together with tau_R>0 gives the exponential-growth-rate bound used here directly.

honest_caveats: This is standard linear ODE theory (variation of constants for a linear system with a locally integrable forcing term) applied to an already-registered equation, not a novel piece of mathematics. The proof was checked by hand/algebraically by this session (the substitution I_R=e^{-tL_R/tau_R}I_0 + ... into the ODE, and the norm bound via the triangle inequality and ||e^{-tL_R/tau_R}||<=e^{t||L_R||/tau_R}, both verify correctly) but NOT machine-checked in Coq. Tier is Dr (a checkable analytical result, independently re-derivable), explicitly NOT Th_coqc.

The result says nothing about the continuum Navier-Stokes PDE itself. It bounds a SEPARATE, finite-dimensional retained state I_R(t) that a not-yet-constructed map r_R: D_NS -> R^m would read off a Navier-Stokes domain state (per the source's Section 5's own explicit disclaimer: 'Equation (16) is not identified with (NS)'). The paper's own Theorem 8.1/Corollary 8.2 (registered here as aliases) states the correct direction of the implication: IF the retained model's regularity hypotheses H_R(T*) continue to hold at a hypothetical Navier-Stokes breakdown time, THEN the retained layer does not blow up -- this is a conditional statement, not a resolution of whether H_R actually survives contact with a genuine Navier-Stokes translation, which remains completely open and is not claimed to be closed by this registration.

The state-dependent generalization (L_R depending on I_R itself, source Section 9) is explicitly flagged by the source as a separate, harder problem NOT covered by this continuation theorem -- do not extend this proposal's tier or claim to that case.
